method_note: Structured index over docs/research/counseling-intelligence/06-major-family-evidence/*.md (both branches -- this branch's 11 families and the peer branch's 9, read directly from its worktree at .claude/worktrees/counseling-intelligence-research-013956/). This file answers the mission brief's deliverable #11 (a machine-readable structured artifact for the interest -> major/field -> skills -> experiences -> career-family -> next-action chain) in a way rules.json (rule registry) and sources.json (citation registry) do not, since neither encodes the taxonomy graph itself. This is an INDEX, not a replacement for the prose docs -- every family's source_doc field points to the authoritative detail; resolve any specific factual claim there, not here. No new research was performed to build this file; every field traces to content already established in the corresponding family document. Per-family sourcing/confidence/limitations live in that document's own Sources table and in sources.json, not duplicated here. family_id '*' in interdisciplinary_connections denotes a structural one-to-many exception (currently only family 18, Education), not a normal pairwise link. Each family's `unsafe_inferences` field extracts that document's own "unsafe inferences" guidance (peer branch's explicit section heading) or equivalent RULE-COUNSEL-tagged cautions (this branch's inline convention) -- directly serves the peer branch's own 13-implementation-readiness.md item 11/12: a ready-made list of things a family-aware explanation template should actively avoid saying.

onboarding_vocabulary_gaps.note: lib/validation/onboarding.ts's INTEREST_SUGGESTIONS has 16 free-text-suggest values (never a closed enum). Families 17, 18, 19, 20 and chemistry/journalism/film/sociology/philosophy/IR/product-design/sustainability-specifically have NO dedicated onboarding suggestion -- reachable only via an approximate-neighbor suggestion or free text.

interdisciplinary_combinations.combination: CS + economics (algorithmic markets, computational social science)
Politics + economics (political economy, public policy analysis)

families.name: Computing & Information Sciences
core_skills: written and oral communication (often underweighted by students)
linear algebra and statistics (ML/AI subfield specifically)

career_families.name: machine learning/AI research and applied ML engineering

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: CS + economics (computational social science, algorithmic markets)

licensure.summary: No general licensure requirement in US/UK/EU/Turkey; narrow exceptions for safety-critical embedded systems or PE-titled 'software engineer' roles in a small number of US jurisdictions.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Introductory personal project (script/website/small game); beginner-friendly online course; sampling more than one subfield lightly.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Sustained project with real scope; open-source contribution; competitive programming (algorithmic evidence, distinct from build evidence); hackathon (distinct rapid-build/teamwork evidence).

distinctive_findings: CS is an umbrella term spanning at least 3 evidence-distinct subfields (software eng, data/ML, theory) that should not be treated as one signal.
Sustained build, algorithmic competition, and hackathon are three distinct, non-interchangeable evidence types within this one family.

country_coverage.turkey: high (İŞKUR official future-occupations list, direct fetch)

unsafe_inferences: Treat 'Computer Science' as one skill, not an umbrella -- a competitive-programming-inclined student and a product-building-inclined student are developing measurably different things (RULE-COUNSEL-203).

Treat sustained build, algorithmic competition, and hackathon participation as one undifferentiated 'did something CS-related' signal -- they demonstrate three distinct, non-interchangeable skills (RULE-COUNSEL-204).

families.name: Mathematics & Statistics
core_skills: statistical software and experimental design (statistics track)

credential_gated_career.name: Actuarial science
credential_gated_career.mechanism: Passing a defined multi-year SOA/CAS (US/Canada) or IFoA (UK) exam sequence, not a specific university major -- university coursework earns exam-credit (VEE) rather than being a mandatory prerequisite.

licensure.summary: No licensure for mathematician/statistician roles generally. Actuarial credentialing (ASA/FSA or IFoA) is a voluntary professional-recognition exam sequence, not government-issued licensure.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Accessible math competitions (school/regional AMC-style); an accessible applied modeling project; general statistics exposure via a real-data school project.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: National/international olympiad tracks (pure-math evidence, not equivalent to applied/stats fit); a modeling or data-analysis project with a real dataset; the first preliminary SOA/CAS actuarial exam (open pre-degree).

distinctive_findings: Actuarial science is a clean, well-documented major≠career example: credentialed by exams, not a mandated major.
The first actuarial exam is one of the few pre-university opportunities in this whole taxonomy with an unambiguous, third-party-administered outcome.

country_coverage.eu: medium (ESCO + Actuarial Association of Europe, not per-country)
country_coverage.turkey: none (not independently verified)

unsafe_inferences: Treat a stated 'I like math' interest as one signal -- it may mean pure/abstract, applied/modeling, or data-analysis, which predict different downstream fits (RULE-COUNSEL-205).
Treat olympiad/competition success as equivalent evidence for applied-math or statistics fit -- it specifically evidences pure-math/proof-based problem-solving, not the other tracks.

families.name: Physical Sciences

licensure.summary: No general licensure for physicist/chemist roles. UK offers a voluntary Chartered Chemist/Chartered Scientist career-long recognition track, not an entry gate.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Accessible hands-on experiment or small build; science-fair participation at an accessible level.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: US National Chemistry Olympiad (multi-tier, ACS-run); ACS Project SEED (paid summer research for economically disadvantaged students); physics olympiad track; a sustained bench or computational research project.

distinctive_findings: A substantial share of quantitative-finance hires come from physics/math degrees specifically, not finance/economics -- a well-documented major≠career pattern.
ACS Project SEED is a specifically cost-accessible paid research pathway, directly relevant to minor-safe/accessible-by-default product philosophy.

country_coverage.turkey: low (İŞKUR names Kimyager only, no physics entry)

unsafe_inferences: Treat a stated physics/chemistry interest as one thing without probing whether the student means theoretical/mathematical or hands-on/experimental work -- these reward different exploration experiences (RULE-COUNSEL-206).

families.name: Life Sciences
mission_raw_fields: neuroscience (research-science reading only; behavioral/clinical reading is family 11)

career_families.name: pre-clinical pathway toward medicine (not a guarantee)

licensure.summary: No general licensure for biological-science research roles. The licensure-heavy adjacent destination is clinical practice (family 10), explicitly out of this family's scope.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Accessible hands-on project (school-supervised experiment, citizen-science contribution, nature-observation/field project).
exploration_pathways.phase_2: International Biology Olympiad (theoretical + hands-on practical exams, 70+ countries); sustained lab-based or field-based research project with a named mentor; structured pre-college research/lab-exposure program.

distinctive_findings: A biology major is necessary for essentially no clinical health profession in most systems -- pre-med 'requirements' are courses, not a mandated major, a common real misconception worth actively countering.

country_coverage.uk: medium-high (Biologist profile via aggregator, not NCS domain directly)
country_coverage.turkey: none (not independently verified)

unsafe_inferences: Treat 'biology' as one activity profile -- it spans wet-lab, field/ecological, and computational work with genuinely different day-to-day activity (RULE-COUNSEL-207).

Imply a biology major is required for medicine or another clinical health profession -- pre-med 'requirements' are specific courses, not a mandated major, a common real misconception (RULE-COUNSEL-208).

families.name: Engineering — Mechanical, Civil, Aerospace, Electrical

career_families.name: patent law (technical background feeding IP law)

credential_gated_career.name: Professional Engineer (US) / Chartered Engineer (UK) / chamber registration (Turkey) / Ingenieur title (Germany)
credential_gated_career.mechanism: Four genuinely distinct national models -- see licensure field. Not one global 'engineers need a license' claim.

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Electrical engineering + CS (computer engineering, embedded systems, signal processing for ML)
Mechanical/electrical engineering + design (product/industrial design, human factors)
Any of the four + environmental science (sustainable/environmental engineering)

licensure.summary: Four distinct national models, the package's canonical licensure comparison: US PE licensure gates specific PRACTICE (stamping public infrastructure), triggered by activity not job title; UK Chartered Engineer (CEng) is competence-based professional recognition layered on an unrestricted right to practice; Turkey's TMMOB chamber registration is required to PRACTICE the profession at all (title + practice gate); Germany's Ingenieurgesetz protects only the TITLE 'Ingenieur', leaving practice itself unregulated.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Accessible build project (simple mechanical/electronic build, introductory robotics/CAD), general physics/math coursework engagement.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Sustained build project with a working, tested result (single strongest evidence type in this family); robotics competitions; structured pre-college engineering program; for civil-leaning students, a project engaging a real local infrastructure problem.

distinctive_findings: The four-country licensure comparison (US/UK/Turkey/Germany) is the canonical illustration, across this whole package, of why licensure framing must always be country-specific.
Many mechanical/electrical/aerospace engineers in large private companies practice a full career without a PE license -- licensure necessity depends on role/industry, not subfield alone.

Casper (the same situational-judgment admissions test found reaching teacher-education, family 18) is confirmed for undergraduate engineering admissions too -- Western University (Canada), Fall 2024, ~7,500 annual applicants -- a fourth confirmed instance of the cross-family SJT pattern and directly relevant to ORYN's population.

country_coverage.eu: medium (ESCO; licensure is member-state-specific, not mapped per-country)
country_coverage.turkey: high (TMMOB official, Law No. 3458/6235)

unsafe_inferences: Encourage a student to commit to one of the four engineering subfields (ME/CE/AE/EE) before sampling more than one's actual design/build activity -- 'Engineering' is as broad as 'Computer Science' or 'Biology' (RULE-COUNSEL-209).

Infer PE-licensure necessity from subfield alone -- it depends on role/industry (public-safety-facing practice vs. large-private-employer roles), and many engineers practice a full career without one (RULE-COUNSEL-210).

Apply one country's engineering-licensure framing to a student targeting a different country -- US/UK/Turkey/Germany are four genuinely distinct models (practice-gated / competence-based / practice-gated-at-the-title-level / title-only) (RULE-COUNSEL-227, RULE-COUNSEL-241).

families.name: Biomedical Engineering
core_skills: analyzing information / solving complex problems in biological systems
translating a clinical/biological need into an engineering specification (the field's defining cross-disciplinary skill)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Boundary with clinical practice (not a pre-med substitute)

licensure.summary: No personal clinical licensure for biomedical engineers themselves. What applies instead is PRODUCT/device regulation (FDA in the US, UKCA/CE marking in UK/EU) -- constrains what the product must demonstrate, not what credential the engineer must personally hold.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Combine an engineering-building activity with a biology-adjacent one -- this field rewards comfort with both sides even at an introductory level.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: A project genuinely combining both (assistive-device build, biomechanics measurement, health-data analysis) is stronger evidence than either alone; a dedicated biomedical/bioengineering research program is the most direct single exploration opportunity.

distinctive_findings: Biomedical engineering is NOT a subset of pre-med -- graduates mostly go into engineering/industry/research roles, not clinical practice; a student wanting to become a physician does not need this degree.
UK 'Biomedical Scientist' (lab-diagnostics role) and this family's 'biomedical engineering' are a real, easily-confused naming overlap that must not be silently conflated.

Turkey's TMMOB chamber jurisdiction for this field, previously genuinely unresolved, is now confirmed: biomedical engineering sits under EMO (electrical engineering chamber) with its own dedicated internal commission.

country_coverage.uk: high (National Careers Service, Clinical Engineer profile)
country_coverage.turkey: high (EMO's own official page confirms biomedical engineering as a dedicated branch of TMMOB's electrical-engineering chamber, resolving what was previously genuinely unresolved)

unsafe_inferences: Counsel biomedical engineering as a 'pre-med' pathway or a subset of one -- it is an engineering discipline whose graduates mostly go into engineering/industry/research, not clinical practice (RULE-COUNSEL-211).
Conflate the UK's 'Biomedical Scientist' (a lab-diagnostics/clinical-science role) with 'biomedical engineering' -- a real, easily-confused naming overlap.

families.name: Economics & Finance
core_skills: critical thinking (per the Fed Challenge's own framing)

career_families.name: financial analysis / investment banking / asset management

credential_gated_career.name: Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
credential_gated_career.mechanism: Postgraduate professional credential via a structured exam program, not a specific undergraduate major -- economics, finance, math, engineering and other quantitative majors all commonly feed into it.

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Economics + business/entrepreneurship (related but distinct: theory/data vs. operational)

licensure.summary: No general licensure for economist/financial-analyst job titles. Specific finance sub-roles (e.g. US securities roles) require firm-sponsored FINRA exams, structurally different from CFA's voluntary credential or PE/medical/legal licensure.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: General coursework engagement; accessible personal-finance or basic-economics project; following real economic events with growing sophistication.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Federal Reserve's High School Fed Challenge (grades 9-12, no prior economics required); National Economics Challenge; independent research project on real economic data; sustained portfolio-tracking project with genuine analytical reflection.

distinctive_findings: A student drawn to economics only for its news/policy relevance, with no appetite for the statistics/econometrics underneath, is a real, worth-surfacing mismatch signal -- milder than an unsafe inference, but a real counselor conversation.

The UK's Government Economic Service is a single, named, 3,500+-economist cross-government career community with no precise US analogue -- and its Fast Stream route has a concrete, checkable 50%-economics-content threshold for combined degrees.

country_coverage.turkey: none (not independently verified)

unsafe_inferences: Treat a student drawn to economics purely for its news/policy relevance, with no appetite for the underlying statistics/econometrics, as a good fit without surfacing the mismatch -- real, worth a counselor conversation, though milder than a disqualification (RULE-COUNSEL-212).

families.name: Business, Management & Entrepreneurship

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Business + law (corporate law, IP strategy for a venture)

licensure.summary: No general licensure for management, business, or entrepreneurship roles. Accounting's CPA credential is a narrow, real exception not elaborated in depth (flagged as a possible future addition).

exploration_pathways.phase_1: General exposure to how organizations operate (a small managed project, an accessible business-simulation activity), joining a business-oriented club.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: DECA/FBLA (US) -- but split by event type: role-play/simulation events demonstrate applied business reasoning, NOT entrepreneurship evidence; DECA's Business Operations Research Events are closer to `research` dimension evidence. Young Enterprise Company Programme (UK) genuinely clears the real-venture bar (real bank account, real sales) unlike DECA/FBLA simulations.

distinctive_findings: Entrepreneurship (originating/testing a new venture) and general business/management study (operating/improving an existing one) are distinct constructs -- a strong management profile is not automatically entrepreneurship evidence.
A large fraction of successful venture founders/operators hold degrees entirely outside business -- this family has one of the loosest major↔career relationships in the whole taxonomy.
DECA/FBLA (simulated scenarios) and UK's Young Enterprise (real venture, real money, real customers) are evidence-quality-distinct, not interchangeable, despite surface similarity.

country_coverage.eu: low (Junior Achievement Europe named as a discovery lead only, not verified)
country_coverage.turkey: medium (İŞKUR names 5 business-adjacent occupations, no DECA-equivalent found)

unsafe_inferences: Treat a strong management/operational profile as automatic evidence of entrepreneurial capability, or vice versa -- these are distinct constructs (RULE-COUNSEL-213).

Treat DECA/FBLA-style simulated business-scenario competition placement as entrepreneurship evidence -- it is a simulation of a business scenario, not the operation of a real one, unlike the UK's Young Enterprise Company Programme which genuinely clears that bar (RULE-COUNSEL-214, RULE-COUNSEL-229).

Present Casper's business-education marketing as evidence a current business-interested high schooler will encounter it -- the one confirmed adopter (Dalhousie's MBA program) is graduate-level, a decade or more past ORYN's population's actual admissions stage (RULE-COUNSEL-245).

families.name: Environmental Science & Sustainability
core_skills: physical stamina (conservation-track specifically, distinctive among every family surveyed)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Environmental science + engineering (sustainable/environmental engineering, renewable energy)
Environmental science + chemistry/physics (environmental chemistry, atmospheric science)

licensure.summary: No general personal licensure for environmental scientist/conservation-scientist roles. Environmental engineering inherits family 05's PE-licensure structure where public infrastructure/safety is involved -- not a separate system.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Accessible citizen-science contribution (biodiversity count, air/water quality monitoring) -- peer-reviewed research supports this as a genuine entry point, not busywork.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Sustained fieldwork or research placement (habitat restoration, invasive-species removal, ecosystem monitoring); mentor-paired applied environmental question projects (named example programs are discovery leads only, not independently verified this pass).

distinctive_findings: This family is unusually receptive to students from OTHER science/engineering majors who specialize into an environmental application later -- often a specialization layered onto another core major, not its own dedicated major.
"Environmental science" and "sustainability" are not the same activity profile (fieldwork/conservation vs. policy/business practice) despite sharing one onboarding anchor.

country_coverage.eu: low (ESCO + EU environmental law noted as existing, not characterized)
country_coverage.turkey: medium (İŞKUR names 2 relevant occupations)

unsafe_inferences: Treat 'environmental science' and 'sustainability' as the same activity profile -- fieldwork/conservation and policy/business practice are both legitimately in this family but reward different exploration experiences (RULE-COUNSEL-215).

Present named teen environmental research/mentorship programs surfaced in this research as confirmed, current opportunities -- they are discovery leads for the separate opportunity-acquisition pipeline to verify, not pre-verified.

families.name: Medicine & Clinical Health Pathways
core_skills: sustained patient/clinical exposure with reflection (not raw hours)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Biomedical engineering boundary (not a substitute for clinical practice)
Life sciences as common pre-clinical (not required) coursework base

licensure.summary: US: MD + residency (not detailed in this doc's HS-stage focus). UK: GMC-recognized degree + foundation + specialist training. Germany: ~6-year Medizinstudium + Staatsexamen -> Approbation (protects 'Arzt/Ärztin' title); Kenntnisprüfung alternate route for foreign-trained doctors.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Shadowing (where a school/family connection or pre-college program can arrange it) and age-appropriate (14-16+) hospital/clinic volunteering -- NOT the adult-clinical-role list (CNA/EMT/scribe), which is realistically 18+.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Sustained shadowing/volunteering with reflection; structured pre-college health programs; self-directed or structured health/bio-science research (process over output).

distinctive_findings: Undergraduate-stage pre-med guidance (MCAT/GPA benchmarks, adult clinical roles) does not map 1:1 onto ORYN's actual 14-18 population -- this document deliberately re-scopes it rather than repeating it uncritically.
Absence of clinical hours for a grade 9-10 student is often an access-gating artifact (many hospital volunteer programs set a minimum age 14-16), not a motivation gap.

country_coverage.us: medium (consensus advising sources, no single official AAMC checklist)
country_coverage.turkey: high (İŞKUR names 5 medicine/allied-health occupations)

unsafe_inferences: Treat 'no clinical hours' as a weakness for a grade 9-10 student -- the realistic HS pathway (shadowing/volunteering) is itself often age-gated (minimum age ~14-16 at many institutions).
Cite a specific MCAT score or pre-med GPA threshold to a high-school-stage student -- these are an undergraduate/professional-school concern entirely outside this population (RULE-COUNSEL-034).
Require research to 'prove' medical interest -- research is common but not universal even among successful undergraduate applicants, let alone required for a high schooler still exploring.

families.name: Psychology & Behavioral/Cognitive Science
mission_raw_fields: neuroscience (behavioral/clinical reading; research reading is family 04)
core_skills: research design across sub-fields (survey, observational, literature synthesis -- genuinely lower access barrier than lab/bench science)

credential_gated_career.name: Clinical/therapeutic psychology practice
credential_gated_career.mechanism: UK: postgraduate doctorate (DClinPsych) after an undergraduate psychology degree. Germany: Approbation under the Psychotherapeutengesetz -- a LEGAL distinction that applies only to the clinical/therapeutic track, not research or non-clinical psychology roles.

licensure.summary: Clinical/therapeutic track specifically is licensure-gated (UK DClinPsych; Germany Approbation under Psychotherapeutengesetz). Research and non-clinical psychology roles are not. Turkey: MEB regulation Art. 3(i) defines 'Psikolog' as requiring a bachelor's-level psychology education (primary-sourced).

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Sampling sub-fields (clinical/social/cognitive/developmental) before committing to one.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: APA High School Summer Internship Program (hands-on research placement); self-directed survey/observational research (genuinely lower access barrier than bench science); peer-support/mental-health-awareness initiatives for the clinical-adjacent track.

distinctive_findings: Psychology is one of the most popular intended majors among selective applicants -- stated interest alone is close to the LEAST differentiating evidence ORYN could recommend around.
A 'no research' gap in psychology specifically has a lower legitimate access excuse than the same gap in bench-science fields, since much of the field's research is genuinely low-access-barrier.

country_coverage.turkey: high (İŞKUR + MEB regulation Art. 3(i), primary source)

unsafe_inferences: Treat 'interest in psychology' alone as meaningful signal -- given the field's popularity, stated interest is close to the least differentiating evidence available; push toward which sub-field and what specific engagement.

Require lab access for legitimate psychology-track research evidence -- much of the field's research (survey design, observational studies, literature synthesis) is genuinely accessible without institutional lab access, a lower access barrier than bench-science fields (RULE-COUNSEL-037).

families.name: Political Science, IR & Public Policy
core_skills: evidence-based argumentation (data, historical precedent, treaties, statistics)
real-world civic/policy engagement (distinct from simulation skill)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Politics + economics (political economy, public policy analysis)
Heavy evidence-type overlap with law-oriented pathways (MUN/debate)

licensure.summary: No licensure for this family. No single NCS profile represents it cleanly (maps to many roles); no İŞKUR match found (list skews technical/vocational).

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Model UN participation; school politics/civics club.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: MUN committee chair/officer roles PAIRED with real-world engagement (campaign/government internship, public-comment participation, published policy writing, civic-organization volunteering) -- MUN alone is simulated argumentation, not equivalent to real policy engagement.

distinctive_findings: MUN is the dominant evidence channel in this family but is explicitly a SIMULATION -- a strong MUN record should never be treated as sufficient on its own without real-world-engagement evidence alongside it.
Campaign/government/NGO internships are frequently geography-gated (proximity to a capital/office) -- absence should not be read as weak interest without considering access.

country_coverage.us: medium (UN official guidance for MUN specifically, not a labor-market source)
country_coverage.uk: low (no single NCS profile, category-browse only)
country_coverage.turkey: none (no İŞKUR match found, honestly reported as a gap)

unsafe_inferences: Treat a MUN 'Best Delegate' award as equivalent evidence to real policy engagement -- it demonstrates simulated argumentation skill, real but narrower than the field itself.

Assume access to campaign/government/NGO internships is universal -- these are frequently geography- and age-gated; absence of this evidence type should not be read as weak interest without considering access (RULE-COUNSEL-040).

families.name: Law-Oriented Pathways

career_families.name: judge, prosecutor, senior civil service (Germany, via Volljurist status)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Engineering + law (technical background into patent law)
Heavy evidence-type overlap with political science (MUN/debate)
Business + law (corporate law, IP strategy for a venture)

licensure.summary: US: no required pre-law major (the family's central finding) -- but law school/bar admission itself is credential-gated. UK: split solicitor/barrister qualification pathways (NCS official). Germany: the package's most exam-intensive model -- Erste Staatsexamen -> 2-year Referendariat -> Zweite Staatsexamen -> Volljurist status (7-11 years total), a single unified state-examined pathway with no US-style 'major now, law school later' flexibility.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Broad humanities/social-science coursework engagement (deliberately not narrowed to one 'correct' major).
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Mock trial, moot court, speech and debate, school law journal (builds the same transferable argumentation/writing skills tested on the LSAT); court observation (public, low-cost access point, unlike most legal internships which are effectively college/law-student-gated).

distinctive_findings: There is no 'pre-law major' in the US/UK sense -- this is the single most important unsafe-inference guard for this family: never imply a student needs to pick a narrow law-track major.

Germany sharpens this finding rather than contradicting it: no mandated undergraduate major, but legal training ITSELF is a single unified state-examined pathway -- a German-track student's decision point differs in kind, not just length, from a US-track one's.

country_coverage.turkey: medium (İŞKUR names Avukat only)

unsafe_inferences: Recommend a specific major as 'the law path' -- there is no required or specifically-rewarded pre-law major in the US/UK sense; this is the single most important unsafe-inference guard for this family (RULE-COUNSEL-041, RULE-COUNSEL-042).
Treat a debate/mock-trial trophy as proof of legal aptitude -- evidence of argumentation skill under a specific competitive format, real but narrower than 'being good at law'.

Assume legal internships are broadly accessible -- most are effectively gated to college-age/law-student applicants; court observation (public, free in most jurisdictions) is a comparatively low-barrier alternative (RULE-COUNSEL-043).

families.name: Sociology, History & Philosophy
core_skills: original argument/research from primary sources or structured reasoning

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: History/philosophy/sociology as common teaching subject-matter majors

licensure.summary: No licensure for this family. No single NCS profile represents it cleanly; no İŞKUR match found (vocational/technical skew).

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Independent reading beyond assignments; a well-developed personal essay/argument.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: National History Day (official, tiered achievement structure: participated -> advanced -> placed); National High School Ethics Bowl (collaborative depth-of-reasoning, distinct from adversarial debate) for philosophy specifically; self-directed research project (sociology, drawing on psychology-family access-aware research framing).

distinctive_findings: National History Day is a rare case where one single activity cleanly demonstrates a full 3-tier achievement ladder (participated/advanced/placed) with official tracking at each level.
Ethics Bowl and debate test meaningfully different things (collaborative reasoning depth vs. adversarial argument) despite surface similarity -- must not be conflated in an explanation.

country_coverage.uk: low (no single NCS profile, category-browse only)
country_coverage.turkey: none (no İŞKUR match found, honestly reported as a gap)

unsafe_inferences: Assume history/philosophy interest requires a competition result to be legitimate evidence -- sustained independent reading or a self-directed research project are real evidence even with zero competitive validation.
Conflate debate-format skill (adversarial) with Ethics-Bowl-format skill (collaborative, depth-of-reasoning judged) -- these test meaningfully different things despite surface similarity.

families.name: Literature, Journalism & Communication
core_skills: reported, edited, substantive writing (quality over unedited volume)
wide reading and craft engagement beyond assignments

licensure.summary: No licensure for this family. No single NCS profile found for journalist/author specifically.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Student/school newspaper involvement; a personal blog with substantive reporting or analysis (not journaling).
exploration_pathways.phase_2: School-paper reporter -> editor progression (a clean escalation pathway); Scholastic Art & Writing Awards (tiered: Gold Key/Silver Key/Honorable Mention, ~330,000 annual submissions -- non-medaling is still real evidence given the pool size); a small number of substantive edited pieces over a large volume of unpublished writing.

distinctive_findings: One of the cleanest real-world confirmations in this whole package of 'quality over quantity': journalism programs explicitly prefer 3-5 strong clips over a longer mediocre list, calling careful selection itself a skill.
The undergraduate-level 'published in an established outlet' bar should be adapted DOWN for high-school stage (school/local outlet), not applied at its literal undergraduate strength.

country_coverage.uk: low (no single NCS profile, category-browse only)
country_coverage.turkey: low (only tangential Dijital Pazarlama/Sosyal Medya Uzmanı matches)

unsafe_inferences: Treat a large volume of unpublished personal writing as equivalent evidence to a smaller set of edited, shared/published work -- careful selection is itself named as a skill by the field's own gatekeepers (RULE-COUNSEL-046).

Require professional/paid publication as a bar for high-school-stage evidence -- the undergraduate-level 'published in an established outlet' bar should be adapted down to school/local-outlet-appropriate evidence.

families.name: Architecture & Design
core_skills: portfolio-documented design thinking and process (not only polished final output)
cross-media exploration (sketches, photography, models, digital -- breadth of medium is valued, not penalized)

career_families.name: interior architect / landscape architect / urban planner (Germany-named variants)

credential_gated_career.name: Licensed/Chartered architect (UK, Germany, and most other EU/regulated jurisdictions)
credential_gated_career.mechanism: Unlike this family's otherwise portfolio-driven, credential-light framing (see distinctive_findings), the professional TITLE "architect" itself is legally protected in the UK (ARB/RIBA, single national regulator) and Germany (16 regional Architektenkammer under a federal Bundesarchitektenkammer) -- a real structural exception, not a portfolio-strength question. Distinct from the biomedical-engineering/actuarial/CFA-style credential_gated_career entries elsewhere in this file (those gate a career FUNCTION via exam/experience; this gates who may legally use a TITLE).

licensure.summary: UK: ARB/RIBA-regulated 'architect' title (single national regulator). Germany: 'Architekt' (and Innenarchitekt/Landschaftsarchitekt/Stadtplaner) protected by law via 16 regional state-level Architektenkammer under a federal Bundesarchitektenkammer -- same protection concept, more fragmented administration than the UK.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Sketching, low-cost self-directed design work -- explicitly NOT gated behind expensive materials or professional software.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: A 10-15-page (or 15-25-project) portfolio spanning assignment-based and self-directed work, explicitly including works-in-progress, not only finished pieces.

distinctive_findings: A thin design portfolio is LESS likely to be a pure access-explained gap than in costlier evidence types elsewhere in this package -- the core low-cost evidence channel (sketching) is broadly accessible.
'Architect' is a legally regulated title in UK/Germany/most EU states -- a real structural exception to this family's otherwise portfolio-driven, credential-light framing.

country_coverage.us: medium (NAAB as accreditation authority marker; portfolio guidance not country-specific)
country_coverage.eu: medium (member states generally regulate similarly to UK, not individually verified)
country_coverage.turkey: high (İŞKUR names 4 relevant occupations, strongest match of any family)

unsafe_inferences: Assume architecture/design evidence requires access to specialized studio space, professional software, or expensive materials -- sketches, collages, and low-cost media are explicitly welcomed alongside professional work (RULE-COUNSEL-049).
Treat unfinished/in-progress work as invalid evidence -- 'works in progress' are explicitly named as acceptable portfolio content.

families.name: Visual & Media Arts
core_skills: storytelling clarity, visual composition, editing choices (film -- explicitly NOT equipment/production value)
process articulation (discussing creative process alongside the work)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Distinct from architecture/design (spatial/functional) though evidence practices overlap
Scholastic Art & Writing Awards is the shared tiered-competition channel for visual-art categories

licensure.summary: No licensure for this family. No single NCS profile found for fine artist/filmmaker specifically.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Sketchbook and in-progress work, explicitly welcomed as evidence, not lesser than 'finished' pieces.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: National Portfolio Day (official, nationwide, feedback-oriented not competitive: 10-12 best/recent pieces); a phone-shot, well-edited short film is legitimate strong evidence -- equipment access is explicitly NOT the differentiator reviewers name.

distinctive_findings: A genuinely important equity finding: film reviewers explicitly name storytelling/composition/editing as differentiating, NOT expensive equipment or production value -- ORYN should never recommend 'get better equipment' ahead of 'tighten the story/edit.'

country_coverage.uk: low (no single NCS profile, category-browse only)
country_coverage.turkey: low (only moderate Grafiker/Teknik Ressam matches)

unsafe_inferences: Suggest production value or equipment quality is a priority evidence gap for film/media work -- storytelling, composition, and editing are what reviewers name as differentiating, not expensive equipment (RULE-COUNSEL-051).
Treat a sketchbook or in-progress work as lesser evidence than a 'finished' piece -- explicitly welcomed by the official portfolio-review standard itself.

families.name: Education & Teaching
mission_raw_fields: not in the mission's original list -- added after both sessions' original families were complete
core_skills: instructional communication (the field's entire core competency, not a secondary skill as in other families)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Education connects to EVERY other family at once (structural exception -- a student's 'what to teach' question routes to whichever subject family matches their interest)

licensure.summary: Unusually clean 3-country comparison, all converging on a 2-part 'degree + separate pedagogical credentialing step' pattern: US state-issued certification/license (Praxis-style exam); UK Qualified Teacher Status (QTS) + 2-year Early Career Teacher induction; Turkey pedagogical formation + KPSS exam, ACTIVELY TRANSITIONING toward a new Milli Eğitim Akademisi requirement (must not be described as static).

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Informal teaching/tutoring of younger students or peers -- a uniquely accessible entry point almost every student has some access to.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Sustained, structured tutoring or teaching-assistant roles -- tests whether a student enjoys the actual instructional act, not just the subject matter (subject-matter achievement alone is NOT teaching-fit evidence).

distinctive_findings: A meaningful share of teachers, especially at university/adult-education level, hold subject-matter degrees (physics, literature) rather than an education-specific degree -- 'the major' is often the taught subject plus a separate pedagogical credential, not one unified 'education major' pipeline.

Turkey's teaching-credential system is actively changing (KPSS alone becoming insufficient, moving toward a National Education Academy requirement) -- must be re-verified against current MEB guidance, not treated as fixed.

A third assessment-type lead from the peer session's medicine research (Casper, a standardized situational-judgment test) generalizes into this family too -- confirmed for teacher-education admissions at 3 Canadian/Australian institutions, surfacing a second, real instance of a recommendation-vocabulary gap neither branch's docs have a type for: 'rehearse a timed situational-judgment response,' distinct from logging an achievement.

country_coverage.turkey: high (MEB regulation, primary source)

unsafe_inferences: Treat 'wanting to teach' as one undifferentiated interest -- elementary generalist, secondary subject-specialist, and special education are substantially different day-to-day work and, in most systems, different credentialing tracks (RULE-COUNSEL-232).

Treat subject-matter achievement (e.g. being good at math) as equivalent evidence to enjoying and being effective at teaching that subject -- a real, family-specific instance of 'subject enthusiasm != the professional activity' (RULE-COUNSEL-233).

Describe Turkey's teaching-credential system as fixed -- it is actively transitioning toward a new Milli Eğitim Akademisi requirement and should be re-verified against current MEB guidance, not treated as static (RULE-COUNSEL-234).

Assume the Casper situational-judgment test applies to a US-target teaching-track student by default -- confirmed used for admission into teacher-education programs at multiple Canadian/Australian institutions (Vancouver Island University, Monash, Brock University), but no US adopter was independently confirmed (RULE-COUNSEL-243).

families.name: Social Work
mission_raw_fields: not in the mission's original list -- peer session found it missing, distinct from psychology's clinical/assessment focus and generic community_impact volunteering
core_skills: emotional resilience (load-bearing, not secondary, per BLS)

career_families.name: community/macro practice (program design, policy, community organizing)

credential_gated_career.name: Licensed clinical social work (US)
credential_gated_career.mechanism: CSWE-accredited MSW plus supervised post-graduate clinical hours (commonly ~3,000 hours/2+ years, state-dependent) and a licensing exam. Broader 'social services' work (case management, program coordination) is more permeable to adjacent degrees (psychology, sociology, public health).

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Social work + psychology (overlapping undergrad prep, diverging professional tracks: assessment/therapy vs. case-management/advocacy)
Social work + education (school social work sits between the two)

licensure.summary: Third clean 3-country comparison in this package, same 2-part pattern as teaching: US (CSWE-accredited MSW + supervised hours + state license); UK (Social Work England registration after an approved qualification); Turkey (MEB regulation Art. 3(p) defines 'Sosyal Çalışmacı' as requiring a bachelor's specifically in social services -- primary-sourced, though the separate associate-degree-titling claim is NOT confirmed by this regulation and remains secondary-only).

exploration_pathways.phase_1: Volunteering with a service organization serving a population the student is drawn to (youth, elderly, homelessness, disability) -- this family's exploration pathway gives that volunteering a specific professional-direction reading rather than a generic community_impact reading.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Sustained (not one-off) volunteering or structured youth-facing programs oriented toward direct service/casework-adjacent work (peer support, hotline/crisis-line volunteering where age-appropriate).

distinctive_findings: A concrete example of the package correcting itself: a primary-source fetch (MEB regulation) confirmed one part of an original claim (bachelor's requirement) while explicitly failing to confirm an adjacent part (associate-degree titling) -- the correct response was to narrow the claim, not treat the partial confirmation as blanket validation.
Sustained, casework-adjacent volunteering is meaningfully stronger evidence for this family than generic episodic volunteering, which only tests general service orientation.

country_coverage.uk: medium-high (NHS Health Careers + licensing-guide sources, not Social Work England's own page directly)
country_coverage.turkey: high (MEB regulation Art. 3(p), primary source)

unsafe_inferences: Treat generic episodic volunteering as equivalent evidence to sustained, casework-adjacent volunteering -- the former only tests general service orientation, the latter tests fit with the actual professional activity (RULE-COUNSEL-096).

Claim primary-source confirmation for the associate-degree-titling distinction in Turkey -- only the bachelor's-requirement half of the original claim was confirmed by the one regulation checked; the rest remains secondary-sourced only, a real example of narrowing a claim rather than treating partial confirmation as blanket validation (RULE-COUNSEL-107).

families.name: Performing Arts & Music
mission_raw_fields: not in the mission's original list -- found missing after confirming family 17 covers only visual arts and film, no music/theater/dance
core_skills: extensive training and regular practice (starts earlier relative to graduation than almost any other family)
physical resilience (dance specifically -- BLS names one of the highest occupational injury/illness rates of any field surveyed)

career_families.name: music therapy (licensed clinical field in some countries)

interdisciplinary_connections.combination: Performing arts + education (teaching an instrument/performance skill)

licensure.summary: No general personal licensure in any of the 3 countries checked. Closest analogue is professional-body membership (UK Equity for actors) -- a chicken-and-egg structure requiring paid work to join the body that helps find paid work, distinct from every licensure system elsewhere in this package.

exploration_pathways.phase_1: General lessons/instruction (already common at this age for this family specifically); school ensemble/theater participation.
exploration_pathways.phase_2: Kennedy Center NSO Young Soloists Competition; Carnegie Hall NYO-USA; a sustained portfolio of recorded/performed work; a formal audition itself, since many conservatory programs weight audition above/alongside academic credentials.

distinctive_findings: This family's core-skill development timeline starts earlier, relative to graduation, than almost any other family -- early sustained specialization is normal and expected here, not a sign of premature narrowing.

Turkey's state conservatories admit via a HYBRID mechanism (a lower TYT score threshold PLUS a talent audition) -- a real, important refinement to the package's general YKS caveat, since this family's admission is not purely exam-score-driven the way most of the rest of Turkey's system is.

Never assume this family's physically-demanding pathways are equally accessible without a stated need, AND never assume a disability precludes this family -- adaptive/disability arts are real, growing practice areas this document did not research in depth but must not be inferred as nonexistent by omission.

country_coverage.turkey: high (state conservatory admission guidance, cross-referenced across multiple official university pages)

unsafe_inferences: Treat 'music' or 'performing arts' as one interest without probing discipline (music/theater/dance) and genre/tradition (classical vs. contemporary) -- these are meaningfully different day-to-day activities and sometimes different admission mechanisms (RULE-COUNSEL-237).

Apply the blanket YKS exam-only caveat to a Turkey-target student interested in this family specifically -- Turkish state conservatories use a hybrid score-threshold-plus-audition mechanism, not pure-score placement (RULE-COUNSEL-238).

Assume this family's physically-demanding pathways (dance especially) are equally accessible to every student without a stated need, OR assume a disability precludes this family -- adaptive/disability arts are real, growing practice areas that must not be inferred as nonexistent by omission (RULE-COUNSEL-240).
Equate this family's aggregate labor-market popularity or wage data with a specific student's individual prospects (RULE-COUNSEL-225).
